I'll think through this year as the farmer myself, then write down the plan.

---

**My thinking (in my own voice):**

Aiya, another year. I'm 63 now and my back doesn't bend like it used to. My husband helps when he can but he's also old. The children are in town working — they send a little money but the farming is mine.

My 12.4 mu is in three pieces. The big flat piece by the road, about 8 mu, that's my wheat-corn land. I've done wheat-corn there for as long as I can remember, like everyone in the village. The other piece, about 4 mu and a bit, I keep in cotton. Cotton is tiring work, especially the picking, but it brings cash money and I've always grown some.

**For my wheat (8 mu):**
I plant after Hanlu (寒露), around the time the cold dew comes — early October. I sow about 30 jin of seed per mu. I buy from the agro-shop, the same variety most people in our village use. Last year's wheat did okay so I'll get the same.

Before planting I spread one bag of compound fertilizer (one 50-jin bag — well, actually one 100-jin bag, 50 kg) on each mu. Then around Qingming, when the wheat starts to joint, I put down some urea, about 30 jin per mu. I don't measure exactly. I walk down the rows and scatter by hand. The big farms put down two bags of compound, but I can't spend that much.

I water 3 times with the well — once before winter to set it, once at jointing, once when the grain is filling. The electricity for pumping costs a lot. If we get good spring rain I skip one watering and save the money.

I spray weed killer once in spring. For diseases I usually don't spray unless the leaves look bad — last year my neighbor sprayed for stripe rust but mine was fine without.

The combine man comes through the village in June and harvests for about 50 yuan per mu. Last year I got around 350 jin per mu (175 kg). Wait — I mean 350 kg per mu. Yes. Sometimes 400 in a good year. This year I'll plan for 350.

**For my corn (8 mu, same land after wheat):**
The hardest part is the turnaround. The day after the wheat combine leaves, I have to get the corn in. The village planter comes with seed and fertilizer in one pass — costs me about 20 yuan per mu plus the seed and fertilizer. I use the hybrid seed the shop sells, whatever variety they have.

The planter puts down one bag of compound with the seed. Then in July, when the corn is about knee-high, I scatter about 30 jin of urea per mu by hand. My back hurts after, but it's quick.

Corn doesn't need as much water as wheat. I irrigate once if it's a dry summer, sometimes twice. Last year was wet enough I only watered once.

I spray herbicide once after planting. For armyworm I spray when I see them — last year was bad. I get around 425 kg per mu most years.

**For my cotton (4.4 mu):**
This is the hard one but it brings cash. I plant in late April when the soil is warm. I lay plastic mulch — the village helps me, costs maybe 50 yuan per mu including the work. I buy commercial cotton seed.

Before planting I put down one bag of compound per mu. Cotton doesn't eat as much as wheat. Then during flowering I scatter a bit of urea, about 20 jin per mu.

I water cotton 2 times — once after planting if it's dry, once when the bolls are filling.

The pesticide is what costs me. Bollworm, pink bollworm, aphids — I spray 4 or 5 times. If I don't spray I lose everything. The shop owner tells me what to mix.

Picking is the killer. Three rounds from August into October. I pick what I can each day. My grandson comes home from town to help me with the last picking. I get about 200 kg of lint per mu, sometimes a bit more.

**Money:**
Adding it all up roughly — seed, fertilizer, the pesticide, the pumping, the combine — it's maybe 7,000 or 8,000 yuan for the whole year. That's a lot for me. If the harvest is bad I have to borrow from my son. So I keep my fertilizer to one bag of compound plus a little urea — that's enough for me.
